standardized.notes: RFC 1055 publication documents an already-used nonstandard.

roles: frame IP datagrams on serial byte streams
addressing: IP addressing is externally configured rather than negotiated by SLIP itself.
error_control: Minimal framing; no generic reliable-link negotiation framework.

operations.diagnostics: Framing errors and serial-link configuration are implementation-specific.
operations.failure_behavior: Mismatched serial parameters or addressing prevent useful connectivity.
operations.operator_interface: Typically configured by OS/network scripts and dialer tooling.

survival.provenance_notes: Historical implementations survive in source archives; later PPP broadly displaced SLIP in managed dial access.

open_questions: Recover BSD/Sun/KA9Q/PC SLIP implementation source and chronology.
Trace CSLIP/Van Jacobson header compression as a separate branch.
Identify named ISP/access-server SLIP deployments before PPP dominance.

related_artifacts.notes: PPP broadly succeeds/generalizes the point-to-point access role but is not a formal RFC revision of SLIP.

notes: SLIP's minimalism is historically meaningful and should not be judged only by later PPP requirements.
